title: Odin: Wisdom Has a Price
subtitle: Knowledge, leadership, and cost in the Prose Edda

learningObjectives.text: Explain that Odin’s authority in the Prose Edda is tied to knowledge, leadership, and costly exchange.
Describe the Prose Edda as a later handbook that preserves and interprets older Norse material.

narrativeBlocks.title: Odin is not just a ruler
narrativeBlocks.body: Odin is the All-Father, but his authority is deeply intellectual: counsel, poetry, foresight, and knowledge gained through risky exchange.

narrativeBlocks.title: The Edda is a later handbook
narrativeBlocks.body: Snorri’s Prose Edda preserves Norse myth while arranging it as guidance for poets. It is invaluable evidence, but not a neutral ancient transcript.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the second source adds
narrativeBlocks.body: The additional corpus record gives a second lens on the same tradition. Compare it with the first source instead of treating either as a complete canon.

narrativeBlocks.title: How to read this evidence
narrativeBlocks.body: Ask what kind of source this is, who translated or organized it, what it can actually prove, and whether another text preserves a different version.

narrativeBlocks.title: Knowledge with a cost
narrativeBlocks.body: In Norse tradition, wisdom is won through exchange, ordeal, and sacrifice. Odin’s power is therefore linked to what he is willing to give up.

quiz.prompt: What best describes the Prose Edda’s role?

choices.text: A medieval handbook that preserves and organizes mythic traditions

quiz.explanation: Snorri’s Prose Edda is invaluable because it preserves mythic material, but it is also a later handbook for poets.

suggestedQuestions: Who wrote the Prose Edda and why?
How does a handbook differ from epic poetry?

quiz.explanation: The Prose Edda presents Odin as an authority associated with counsel, poetry, and costly knowledge.

suggestedQuestions: What does Odin give or risk for knowledge?
